section.title: Running Sanity Tests
section.p: Ant tasks and batch files are provided to generate and run the applications used in the sanity tests. Three application sets are provided. The first set tests the framework as a rich client two tiers application. The second set tests the framework as three tiers application using CORBA. The third set tests the framework as three tiers applicaiton using J2EE/RMI.
The application sets are build using ant targets executing against the build.xml file.
section.note: The build scripts assumes that JDK 1.4.2 and 1.5.0 are installed on the build machine.
The EJB ant task is an extension and needs additional librairies. The BCEL jar file must be installed. Please consult the Ant manual for detailed instructions.
section.p: To run sucessfully the tests the used software packages for the database, CORBA ORB, or J2EE container must be installed. Please refer to the installation notes of the used packages. The application sets are started using shell scripts located in the scripts tests directory.

ul.li:
Rich client tests
Starts the client application test-rich-client.

CORBA three tiers tests
Starts CORBA request broker orb-start.
Starts the CORBA server test-corba-server
Starts the CORBA client test-corba-client

JBoss three tiers tests
Starts the J2EE JBoss container using its start script. The J2EE server was copied in the deployment directory when building it and will start automatically.
Starts the J2EE client test-j2ee-client.

section.p: Please remember that CORBA and J2EE should not be run simultaneously or be very careful to avoid port conflicts.
section.note: If the application does not start, verify first that the middleware is running. If using J2EE verify that the server was correctly deployed and started.

section.title: Sanity Tests
section.p: A set of sanity tests is defined to verify the adequacy and completness of the application. The following cases are defined.
The set of scenarios checks the user interface of the application.

ol.li: Verify that the menu bar is populated with the expected menu items and that a model can be displayed in the explorer window.
Verify the information in the about dialog. The list of librairies, the license, the contributors and the system properties should be visible and up to date.
Verify the information in the preferences dialog. The list of configured cartridges and their configuration should be visible and up to date.

section.p: This set of scenarios checks that the reading and writing of models in all supported formats are working.

ol.li: Load the provided model in the application. Checks that packages, classes, properties and indexed properties are displayed.
Save the model as another ArgoUML model. Load the saved model and verify that packages, classes, properties and indexed properties are displayed.
Save the model as a XML model. Load the saved model and verify that packages, classes, properties and indexed properties are displayed.
Save the model as a serialized model. Load the saved model and verify that packages, classes, properties and indexed properties are displayed.

section.p: This set of scenarios verifies that the provided code generators are working.

ol.li: Load the provided model in the application. Generates all artifacts for all loaded cartridges.

section.p: The generated source code artifacts must now be verified. Build the test applications with the help of the provided ant scritps.

ol.li: Execute the rich client test application. Test it by adding some data objects. Modify the saved objects, and delete some of them.
Execute the CORBA client server test application. Test it by adding some data objects. Modify the saved objects, and delete some of them.
Execute the J2EE JBoss client server test application. Test it by adding some data objects. Modify the saved objects, and delete some of them.

section.title: Quality Assurance
section.p: The quality of the source code artifacts and associated documentation is measured using various open source metrics and check tools. The home page of the project contains links to all used projects.
A release is published only if the sanity tests were sucessful.

An informal rule is that major releases of the applications have no compilation errors or warnings in the Eclipse environment. A second one is that the Java documentation check found no documentation errors on package and class level. The public methods should be documented.
